'''Raymond Gerard Flood''' is Emeritus Fellow and a member of the Continuing Education Department at [[Kellogg College, Oxford]],<ref name="kellogg.ox.ac.uk">{{Cite web |url=http://www.kellogg.ox.ac.uk/raymond-g-flood |title=Raymond G Flood, Kellogg College (accessed 9 June 2014) |access-date=22 January 2015 |archive-date=18 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150218074816/http://www.kellogg.ox.ac.uk/raymond-g-flood |url-status=dead }}</ref> and has been a [[Gresham Professor of Geometry|Professor of Geometry]] at [[Gresham College]].<ref name="gresham.ac.uk">[http://www.gresham.ac.uk/professors-and-speakers/professor-raymond-flood Professor Raymond Flood, Gresham College (accessed 9 June 2014)]</ref>

==Education==
Flood achieved a Bachelor of Science degree at [[Queens University, Belfast]], and a master's degree at [[Linacre College, Oxford]]. He obtained his PhD from [[University College, Dublin]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.statisticsviews.com/details/news/2562621/Raymond-Flood-Appointed-Professor-of-Geometry-at-Gresham-College.html |title=Raymond Flood Appointed Professor of Geometry at Gresham College (accessed 9 June 2014) |access-date=22 January 2015 |archive-date=3 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303223653/http://www.statisticsviews.com/details/news/2562621/Raymond-Flood-Appointed-Professor-of-Geometry-at-Gresham-College.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Flood obtained his doctorate through part-time study, as he had already acquired a family and a job.<ref name="youtube.com">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u1A40oG5jqk Video Interview short with Professor Raymond Flood (accessed 22 January 2015)]</ref>

==Career==
In 1990, Flood was made a Founding Fellow of [[Kellogg College, Oxford]], formally [[Rewley House]]. [[Kellogg College, Oxford]] was created to look after the interests of mature and part-time students. Flood primarily teaches those students who are either mature, or who study part-time.<ref name="youtube.com" /> He has held numerous positions at the College and the [[University of Oxford]], including Curator of the University Libraries and as a University lecturer at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="kellogg.ox.ac.uk" />

Flood has dedicated much of his academic career promoting mathematics and computing to adult audiences. He has been President of the [[British Society for the History of Mathematics]] from 2006 until 2009,<ref>[http://www.dcs.warwick.ac.uk/bshm/RW.pdf 'The British Society for the History of Mathematics'] by [[Robin Wilson (mathematician)|Robin Wilson]] and Raymond Flood in Newsletter of the European Mathematics Society, March 2013, Issue 87</ref> and also Research Associate in the School of Theoretical Physics, [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]].<ref name="kellogg.ox.ac.uk" /> On [[Gresham College]], Flood has said "Gresham College comes from a long tradition of liberal adult education. Allowing people from a variety of backgrounds... to get access to current thinking on the major issues of the day. Gresham College ethos is very similar to my own ethos"<ref name= "videoshort">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jpxm4p0U8fQ Professor Raymond Flood and Gresham College (accessed 22 January 2015)]</ref>

In August 2012, Flood was appointed [[Gresham Professor of Geometry]] at [[Gresham College]] for a period of three years, replacing [[John D. Barrow]].<ref>[http://www.gresham.ac.uk/gresham-professor-of-geometry Gresham Professor of Geometry on www.gresham.ac.uk]</ref> During his term at the College he delivered series of free public lectures on ''Shaping Modern Mathematics'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gresham.ac.uk/shaping-modern-mathematics|title=Shaping Modern Mathematics|publisher=Gresham College|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303205744/http://www.gresham.ac.uk/shaping-modern-mathematics|archive-date=2016-03-03|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''Applying Modern Mathematics'',<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.gresham.ac.uk/applying-modern-mathematics |title=''Applying Modern Mathematics'' series page on www.gresham.ac.uk |access-date=22 January 2015 |archive-date=22 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150122190745/http://www.gresham.ac.uk/applying-modern-mathematics |url-status=dead }}</ref> and ''Great Mathematicians, Great Mathematics''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gresham.ac.uk/great-mathematicians-great-mathematics|title=Great Mathematicians, Great Mathematics|publisher=Gresham College|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303224734/https://www.gresham.ac.uk/great-mathematicians-great-mathematics|archive-date=2016-03-03|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Other research work and publications==
Aside from his academic work, Flood is active in communicating mathematics and its history to non-specialist audiences. He has appeared on [[BBC Radio 4]]'s [[In Our Time (BBC Radio 4)|In Our Time]]<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b009mvj0 ''The Laws of Motion''] and [https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p003hyd9 ''Negative Numbers''] on the BBC In Our Time website (accessed 10 January 2015)</ref> and has lectured on transatlantic voyages with {{RMS|Queen Mary 2}}.<ref name="gresham.ac.uk" />

Flood has produced and co-produced many publications and books on mathematics. Some of the most recent books with which he has been involved are ''James Clerk Maxwell: Perspectives on his Life and Work'' (Oxford University Press, 2014),<ref>[http://ukcatalogue.oup.com/product/9780199664375.do ''Jame Clerk Maxwell: Perspectives on his Life and Work'' listing on the OUP website]</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IMl7AgAAQBAJ | title=James Clerk Maxwell: Perspectives on his Life and Work | isbn=978-0-19-164125-1 | editor=Flood, Raymond | editor2=McCartney, Mark | editor3=Whitaker, Andrew | date=9 January 2014 | publisher=OUP Oxford }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Kidwell, Peggy Aldrich|author-link=Peggy Aldrich Kidwell|date=September 25, 2014|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/james-clerk-maxwell-perspectives-on-his-life-and-work |title=Review of ''James Clerk Maxwell: Perspectives on his Life and Work'', edited by Raymond Flood, Mark McCartney and Andrew Whitaker|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America }}</ref> ''The Great Mathematicians'' (Arcturus, 2011),<ref>{{cite book|author=Flood, Raymond|author2=Wilson, Robin|title=The Great Mathematicians: Unravelling the Mysteries of the Universe|year=2011|publisher=Arcturus Publishing|isbn=978-1-84858-416-7|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fIkEAwAAQBAJ|postscript=; e-book}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1017/S0025557200006240 |title=Review of ''The great mathematicians'', by Raymond Flood and Robin Wilson. Pp. 208. 2011 {{text|ISBN:}} 9871848379022 (Arcturus) |date=2013 |last1=Leversha |first1=Gerry |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |volume=97 |issue=539 |pages=361–362 |s2cid=233357933 }}</ref> and ''Mathematics in Victorian Britain'' (Oxford University Press, 2011).<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=l5YiddUUfl4C | title=Mathematics in Victorian Britain | isbn=978-0-19-960139-4 |lccn=2011938072 |editor=Flood, Raymond | editor2=Rice, Adrian | editor3=Wilson, Robin | date=29 September 2011 | publisher=OUP Oxford }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=May 16, 2014|author=Ruane, P. N.|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematics-in-victorian-britain |title=Review of ''Mathematics in Victorian Britain'' edited by Raymond Flood, Adrian Rice, and Robin Wilson|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America }}</ref><ref>[http://ukcatalogue.oup.com/product/9780199601394.do ''Mathematics in Victorian Britain'' listing on the OUP website]</ref>
